diagnostic_evidence.quote: one can engineer many non-Gaussian $\pi$ with exact affine transports that lie strictly beyond $\mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract omits the weakly y*-dependent restriction: F is defined as the union only over maps whose A and B do not depend on y*. The paper itself later says that fully y*-dependent affine maps can be exact strictly beyond E^EnKU, so the unqualified statement that F is the largest exact set for any measure-dependent affine transport, and the unqualified near-optimality conclusion, is false for the general affine conditioning class.

failure_location.quote: Finally, we ask what the largest possible set of measures  \(\mathrm{F}\) is that any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the abstract claim to weakly y*-dependent affine conditioning maps, the class used to define F, and note that fully y*-dependent updates are outside the claimed maximality; no proof change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Only the summary overstates the optimality regime. Theorem thm:F_char and the discussion remain valid for weakly y*-dependent affine conditioning maps; the false part is the broader advertised scope.
issues.title: Abstract states F is maximal for any affine transport, but F is defined only for weakly y*-dependent maps
issues.why_classification: A local qualifier restores agreement with the definition of F and with the paper's own counterexamples; no theorem, proof, rate, or formal guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a simple consequence of the fact that $X + BY$ is Gaussian and there is an affine transport map between any two non-singular Gaussians.

issues.failure_explanation: For a scalar zero-mean Gaussian pair with Var(X)=Var(Y)=1 and Cov(X,Y)=r in (0,1), exactness of AX+BY+c requires A^2+2ABr+B^2=1-r^2. Completing the square gives (A+Br)^2+(1-r^2)B^2=1-r^2, so a real A exists only when |B|<=1. Taking B=2 gives Cov(X+BY)=5+4r>0 but no real A, contradicting the universal claim.

failure_location.quote: For example, for every choice of $B$ (assuming $\Cov(X+BY)$ has full rank for all $y_\star$) there are $A$  and $c$ such that $L_{\pi, y_\star}(x,y)= A(\pi,y_\star)x + B(\pi,y_\star)y + c(\pi,y_\star)$ is exact.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the sentence to infinitely many admissible B, or state the correct covariance condition that A and B must satisfy; no later result needs repair.
issues.overall_effect: The example overstates the freedom in choosing exact affine Gaussian updates. The true existence of infinitely many such maps, and the later uniqueness and maximality results, are unaffected.
issues.title: Universal claim that every B admits an exact affine Gaussian update is false
issues.why_classification: The correction is a one-sentence restriction or covariance condition; the central ambiguity of the EnKU and all formal results survive.
